title: Modification of an automated precision farming robot for high temporal resolution measurement of leaf angle dynamics using stereo vision
author: Hennecke, Bömer, et al.

steps.title: Place reference plant
steps.instruction: Position the 3‑D printed sugar beet reference model in the cultivation area where the FarmBot will operate.

steps.title: Configure camera viewpoints
steps.instruction: Mount the stereo‑vision camera on the robot and arrange it at the desired number of viewpoints (1, 3, or 6) equally spaced on a circle around the reference model.

steps.title: Acquire point clouds
steps.instruction: For each viewpoint configuration, record three complete point‑cloud datasets at 15‑minute intervals.

steps.title: Reconstruct 3D mesh
steps.instruction: Generate a 3‑D mesh from each recorded point‑cloud set using the chosen reconstruction software; note that the two innermost leaves may not be reconstructed and small edge artifacts may appear.

steps.title: Load clouds into CloudCompare
steps.instruction: Open the reconstructed point‑cloud files in CloudCompare (open‑source point‑cloud processing software).

steps.title: Annotate leaf basis and tip
steps.instruction: For each leaf, use the “Point picking list” tool to click the leaf‑blade basis point and the leaf‑blade tip point, then export their Cartesian coordinates.

substeps.instruction: Open the Point picking list tool.
Select the blade‑basis point and record its (x, y, z) values.
Select the blade‑tip point and record its (x, y, z) values.
Save or copy the coordinate list for later calculations.

steps.title: Calculate leaf angle
steps.instruction: Compute the leaf angle θ for each leaf using the exported coordinates:

substeps.instruction: Compute the vector v from basis to tip: v = (x_tip‑x_base, y_tip‑y_base, z_tip‑z_base).
Project v onto the z‑axis: v_z = z_tip‑z_base.
Calculate the angle: θ = arccos(v_z / |v|) (in degrees).

steps.title: Aggregate and compare measurements
steps.instruction: For each leaf and each time point, record the computed angle; then compare the set of angles (mean of three replicates) to manually collected reference angles to assess accuracy (e.g., mean errors of 7.10° for 1 viewpoint, 3.02° for 3 viewpoints, 2.39° for 6 viewpoints).
